claim: nixpkgs ships an in-tree Mosquitto NixOS VM test at nixos/tests/mosquitto.nix with one server node and two client nodes, structured as { name; nodes; testScript; }.
stance_target: A NixOS test gate for a Rust MQTT agent can crib an existing upstream pattern rather than inventing broker-in-test wiring from scratch
scope_conditions: nixpkgs master branch, nixos/tests/mosquitto.nix, as of fetch 2026-09-02
quoted_support: { name = "mosquitto"; ... nodes = { server = { pkgs, ... }: { networking.firewall.allowedTCPPorts = [ port tlsPort anonPort ]; networking.useNetworkd = true; services.mosquitto = { enable = true; ... listeners = [ ... ]; }; }; client1 = client; client2 = client; }; testScript = '' ... ''; }

claim: The upstream test configures the broker entirely through the services.mosquitto NixOS module options (enable, settings, listeners with per-listener users, acl, passwordFile, hashedPasswordFile), with per-user ACL strings like "read ${topic}" / "write ${topic}".
stance_target: The ephemeral broker in a CI test gate can be declared as NixOS config rather than managed by a process supervisor in the test script
quoted_support: services.mosquitto = { enable = true; settings = { sys_interval = 1; }; listeners = [ { inherit port; users = { password_store = { inherit password; }; ... reader = { inherit password; acl = [ "read ${topic}" "read $SYS/#" ]; }; writer = { inherit password; acl = [ "write ${topic}" ]; }; }; } { port = anonPort; omitPasswordAuth = true; settings.allow_anonymous = true; acl = [ "pattern read #" ]; ... } ]; };

claim: The testScript asserts broker readiness with server.wait_for_unit("mosquitto.service") after start_all(), then exercises pub/sub via the mosquitto_pub/mosquitto_sub CLI clients installed on client nodes through environment.systemPackages.
stance_target: A hardware-daemon test gate can synchronise on mosquitto.service readiness and use stock mosquitto clients as the test harness
scope_conditions: Python testScript in the NixOS test framework
quoted_support: start_all() server.wait_for_unit("mosquitto.service") with subtest("check passwords"): client1.succeed(publish("-m test", "password_store")) ... client = { pkgs, ... }: { environment.systemPackages = with pkgs; [ mosquitto ]; }

claim: The test demonstrates cross-node message-delivery assertion using parallel subscribe/publish with wait_for_console_text on a UUID client id, i.e. subscribing on one client and publishing from the other node.
stance_target: End-to-end MQTT delivery through the ephemeral broker can be asserted deterministically in a two-node NixOS test
quoted_support: parallel( lambda: client1.succeed(subscribe("-i 3688cdd7-aa07-42a4-be22-cb9352917e40", "reader")), lambda: [ wait_uuid("3688cdd7-aa07-42a4-be22-cb9352917e40"), client2.succeed(publish("-m test", "writer")) ] )

claim: The test also covers TLS listeners using snakeoil certificates generated inside the test with pkgs.runCommand + gnutls certtool, and an allow_anonymous listener gated by omitPasswordAuth.
stance_target: Scope reference for what an MQTT CI gate may optionally cover (TLS, anonymous auth)
quoted_support: snakeOil = pkgs.runCommand "snakeoil-certs" { buildInputs = [ pkgs.gnutls.bin ]; ... } ... { port = tlsPort; ... settings = { cafile = "${snakeOil}/ca.crt"; certfile = "${snakeOil}/server.crt"; keyfile = "${snakeOil}/server.key"; require_certificate = true; use_identity_as_username = true; }; }
